Subject: Audit request — SSO session records + key references

Hi Rishi,

Thanks for the quick intro last week. As part of our procurement checklist we need to confirm what session-level audit data Redwood can provide for SSO-authenticated requests, and how KMS key identifiers are surfaced in logs when BYOK is used.

Specifically HealthWorks needs:
- Per-session records (session_id, authn_time, user_id/email, tenant_id) for 90 days
- Evidence that KMS key_id or key fingerprint is included in request metadata for any encrypted-at-rest artifacts
- An example log sample (redacted) showing the fields and format

I've attached a redacted session sample and a short table of HealthWorks minimum fields. Can you confirm feasibility and any gaps within Hosted vs Dedicated deployments? Also call out any privacy or PII redaction tradeoffs you anticipate.

Appreciate a response by EOD Thursday if possible — we have an internal gating review Friday.

Thanks,
Emily
--
Emily Grant
Security Engineering Manager — HealthWorks

Subject: Re: Audit request — SSO session records + key references

Emily — thanks for the clear list and the sample. Looping in Product (Marissa), Ops (Grace) and Security (Ben) to triage. Quick answers up-front: we can provide session_id, timestamps, user/tenant identifiers and IP blocks in logs for Hosted and Dedicated; the formatting differs slightly across runtimes. BYOK KMS key_id exposure is supported in Dedicated today; for Hosted we currently surface a key alias token (opaque) and can add a key fingerprint in logs as an engineering change.

Marissa / Grace / Ben — can you help scope the work to:
1) Define exact log schema we can commit to (fields + sample payload)
2) Decide retention policy knobs (90 days default, carveouts for PII) + product UX for retention windows
3) Confirm telemetry differences Hosted vs Dedicated and any timeline for exposing key fingerprint in Hosted logs

I started a ticket SEC-4921 (link below) and attached a KMS rotation matrix I pulled from Infra for reference. Emily — noted the Friday review — we'll aim to get a proposed scope by Thursday EOD.

Links: https://redwood-internal.atlassian.net/browse/SEC-4921
Attachments: kms-rotation-matrix.xlsx

—Rishi

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-11T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Audit request — SSO session records + key references

Thanks for the tag, Rishi. A few product-level constraints / proposals:
- Schema: propose base fields = [session_id, user_id, tenant_id, auth_method, auth_time, expires_at, ip_cidr, user_agent, request_path, response_code]. We should include a "key_reference" optional field that can be token/alias or fingerprint depending on deployment.
- Retention: default 90d for session records. For PII (email / user display name) we should support an anonymized flag (hash) and a short-term carveout flow (30d) for customers who request minimal exposure.
- Hosted vs Dedicated: Hosted will expose "key_reference_alias" (opaque) in GA Q4; Dedicated can show key_id/fingerprint immediately but requires key owner consent for sharing in some contracts.

Questions for Security / Ops:
- Ben — for SOC2 evidence, do you need raw session payloads or summarized audit artifacts (audit_lines + signed hash)?
- Grace — does the rotation matrix imply any changes to log fields when keys rotate? If so, define migration strategy.

I can prepare a sample log schema doc and lightweight migration note by Wednesday. If product agrees to the anonymized/short-term carveout approach, we can present that to HealthWorks Friday.

-Marissa
Senior PM — Redwood Console
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-12T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Audit request — Audit evidence needs (SSO session level)

Quick security input: for external audit we usually need tamper-evident artifacts. My recommendation:
- Provide raw session record export (redacted) + per-batch signed digest (SHA256) that we can sign with an internal key for short-term evidence; that covers auditors without exposing raw PII beyond what the customer consents to.
- Required fields (min): session_id, user_hash (sha256 of user_id), tenant_id, auth_time, auth_method, ip_cidr (no precise IP if customer requests), key_reference (alias or fingerprint), event_type (login/refresh/revoke), request_id.
- KMS rotation: include a "key_rotation_epoch" and "key_previous_ref" when rotation happens so auditors can trace which key encrypted what at any point in time.

If we expose fingerprints in Hosted, we need a quick opt-in legal addendum for customers who bring keys to Hosted; ops will need a migration plan.

Ben
Security Engineering — Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Emily Grant <emily.grant@healthworks.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: SSO session audit scope & KMS handling — decision request

Emily — summary and decision request below. Internal owners / deadlines listed so HealthWorks has a single point of contact.

Summary of agreed approach (proposal):
- Log schema draft: Marissa will publish a schema (fields + sample payload) that includes optional "key_reference_fingerprint" and mandatory audit fields. (owner: Marissa, due: 2026-07-22)
- Retention & PII: Default 90d; support anonymized user_hash and a short-term 30d carveout on request. Legal/Contracts will need an opt-in flag for Hosted if we expose fingerprints. (owner: Marissa + Legal, due: 2026-07-24)
- KMS exposure: Dedicated: full key_id/fingerprint available immediately. Hosted: surface alias by default; add fingerprint as engineering change synchronized with an addendum. Ops to prepare rotation migration notes. (owner: Grace, due: 2026-07-29)
- Audit evidence: provide redacted raw exports + signed digest bundles for auditor review. (owner: Ben, due: 2026-07-26)

Action items for HealthWorks: please confirm that the schema + carveout approach meets your review criteria by 2026-07-23 so we can commit timelines. If you need the Hosted fingerprint sooner, let us know — we'll escalate but will need a contractual opt-in.

Emily: FYI I'm attaching the redacted sample you provided and our current KMS matrix for transparency.

Thanks all — happy to run a 30 minute sync if helpful.

—Rishi
Product Ops — Redwood Inference
